title: 20100627.creek.paddling.wav
author: dobroide
changes: Real recording of splashing and paddling through a small babbling creek near Aznalcóllar, Spain, used for the platypus: platypuses are almost silent, and the sound most tied to them is water splashing in the creeks where they paddle and dive (no free recording of a platypus itself was found; the paddler here is a person wading). Trimmed to 0.70–3.60 s of the original, mixed to mono, silence trimmed, loudness-normalised (≈ −18 dBFS RMS, peak ≤ −1 dBFS), peaks limited by 1.6 dB, 10 ms fade-in / 120 ms fade-out, encoded as 96 kbps mono MP3. Taken from the Freesound high-quality MP3 preview of the recording.
